research_mode: official Home Office 2026 technical annex only; transferred-or-cancelled reasons, comparison boundaries and recording standards; no parcel result or safety score claimed

sources.name: Transfer outside force jurisdiction
verified_claims: a recorded crime can be transferred when committed outside the recording force's jurisdiction
the record is passed to the appropriate force
transfer is distinct from cancellation
limitations: transfer volume depends partly on force geography and boundaries
a transfer is not evidence that no crime occurred

sources.name: Cancellation after verifiable no-crime information
verified_claims: a record can be cancelled when additional verifiable information shows no notifiable crime occurred
the decision follows initial crime recording
the reason is separately classified
limitations: cancellation is a recording-rule decision rather than a court finding
the reason must not be merged with duplication or error

sources.name: Duplicate-record cancellation
verified_claims: a record can be cancelled as a duplicate
it can also be part of a crime already recorded
the cancellation prevents double counting
limitations: duplicate status requires auditable linkage
duplicate cancellation is not proof that the underlying event was invalid

sources.name: Recorded-in-error cancellation
verified_claims: crime recorded in error is a distinct cancellation reason
it is separately reported from duplicate and no-notifiable-crime reasons
the initial record is later corrected through the cancellation process
limitations: error cancellation must not be generalized to force-wide accuracy
the category count is process evidence rather than parcel evidence

sources.name: Specified self-defence cancellation
verified_claims: self-defence is one of the five cancellation reasons
the category applies to specified recorded assaults
it is separately classified from other cancellation reasons
limitations: the category is offence-scope limited
it must not be inferred where the official cancellation reason is absent

sources.name: Pre-April-2015 combined no-crime return
verified_claims: before April 2015 forces supplied transfers and cancellations as one combined category
the return was formerly described as no-crimes
reason-level detail was unavailable
limitations: pre-2015 totals cannot be decomposed into the five later reasons
historical comparison requires aggregation to a common scope

sources.name: Full reason comparison after March 2016
verified_claims: full reason-level comparison is possible only for recent years after March 2016
earlier comparison is limited to the total of the five categories
the framework transition constrains time series
limitations: reason-level trends must not be backcast into the combined-return period
edition and force coverage still require validation

sources.name: Twenty-four-hour crime-recording standard
verified_claims: from April 2015 the counting rules required recording at the earliest opportunity
the maximum was 24 hours after the recording decision
the previous maximum was 72 hours
limitations: the rule change can increase later transfers or cancellations
the standard is not a guarantee that every record is entered within the limit

sources.name: Local-practice effect on transfer volumes
verified_claims: forces can differ in how quickly they initially record crimes
immediate recording can lead to more later transfers or cancellations
transfers are especially susceptible to local practice
limitations: cross-force differences may reflect process rather than crime levels
recording-practice metadata is required for interpretation

sources.name: Neutral interpretation of high or low transfer counts
verified_claims: high or low transferred-or-cancelled volumes are not necessarily positive or negative
force location can affect transfer counts
differences can reflect recording practices
limitations: counts must not be scored as force performance without contextual evidence
geographic and process factors must remain explicit
